advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that calls get_parent_map on a __new__-constructed transport (skipping __init__) to pin the getattr/_MISSING fallback the helper docstring relies on.
evidence: transport.py:518-522: docstring: 'a transport built via __new__ (some pagination tests) skips __init__'s assignment entirely, so a bare read would raise'
tests all build via `def _transport(client): return JiraDataCenterTransport(client=client, project="DC")` — no __new__ path is exercised in this module
The ticket comment records that wiring the bare attribute turned 3 __new__-based pagination tests RED, but those tests live elsewhere, so this module does not pin the getattr behaviour it depends on.
advisory.finding: _resolve_epic_link_field_id's docstring justifies the getattr(self, '_epic_link_field_id', _MISSING) fallback specifically by the '__new__' (skipped __init__) transport case, but no test in the new module constructs a transport via __new__ to exercise that path — every test uses the normal _transport() / __init__ constructor, which always assigns _epic_link_field_id.
scenarios: A future refactor replaces getattr with a bare attribute read; this module stays green while the latent AttributeError regression (the exact one the ticket comment describes) reappears for __new__-built transports.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert get_parent_map passes the discovered Epic Link field id in the search `fields=` argument (capture the `fields=` value in _FakeClient.search_issues and assert it contains _EPIC_FIELD_ID).
evidence: transport.py:562 `search_fields = "parent" if epic_field is None else f"parent,{epic_field}"`
test file _FakeClient.search_issues signature accepts `fields: str | None = None` but the body `return self.issues[startAt : startAt + maxResults]` never inspects it
ABSENCE: no assertion in any test captures/checks the `fields=` string passed to search_issues; test_epic_parent_is_read_back would pass even if the epic field were never requested
advisory.finding: No test asserts get_parent_map actually requests the discovered Epic Link field id in the search `fields=` parameter; the fake client ignores `fields=` and returns the epic value regardless, so dropping `epic_field` from the composed `search_fields` string (which on a real DC would omit the column and make read-back silently return None) would not fail any test.
scenarios: A future edit drops the epic field from the requested fields string; unit suite stays green while live DC read-back silently regresses to None
advisory.suggested_fix: In _FakeClient, record the `fields` argument (e.g. self.last_fields = fields) and add a test asserting `_EPIC_FIELD_ID in client.last_fields` after get_parent_map runs; assert it is absent when has_epic_link=False.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a case where a non-sub-task issue has the Epic Link field present but empty/non-string and assert the parent maps to None.
evidence: transport.py:572-574 `if not parent_key and epic_field and isinstance(fields, dict): epic_value = fields.get(epic_field); parent_key = epic_value if isinstance(epic_value, str) and epic_value else None`
ABSENCE: all epic-value test fixtures use a valid non-empty string (`_EPIC_FIELD_ID: "DC-1"`); no fixture sets the epic field to "", None, or a non-str value
advisory.finding: The empty/non-string Epic Link value guard `parent_key = epic_value if isinstance(epic_value, str) and epic_value else None` is untested: no case exercises an issue whose Epic Link field is present but empty-string or a non-string value, which must map to None (not be emitted as a parent).
scenarios: An issue carries an empty or structured Epic Link value; a regression removing the `isinstance(..., str) and epic_value` guard would emit a bad parent or crash, uncaught
